name: Foundation of Al-Azhar, Islamic University
summary: Fatimid commander Jawhar founds Al-Azhar mosque in Cairo (970) as both a center of Shia Ismaili learning and a congregational mosque. Under subsequent Fatimid caliphs it develops into a teaching institution. After Saladin's conquest (1171) transforms Egypt to Sunni, Al-Azhar shifts to Sunni Shafi'i learning; it eventually becomes the most authoritative Islamic educational institution in the Sunni world.

_quarry.structural_significance: Al-Azhar's 1,050-year continuity makes it the world's oldest continuously operating university; its authority on Islamic legal and theological questions is without parallel in the Sunni world; the institution's original Shia orientation (transformed to Sunni by political conquest) illustrates how institutional continuity can transcend ideological shifts; modern Al-Azhar's statements on Islamic law carry global weight in 1.8 billion-strong Sunni Islam
